program_name: Los Angeles County Measure W (Safe, Clean Water Program)
administering_agency: Los Angeles County Flood Control District / Public Works
statutory_citation: Los Angeles County Flood Control District Code Chapter 16
eligible_improvements: Urban street tree canopy planting with verified 24-hr stormwater runoff capture (min. 85th percentile storm event: 0.75-1.0 in)
Infiltration basins, bio-retention swales, permeable pavers, and curbside rain gardens
Multi-benefit green stormwater infrastructure
funding_share_description: Regional program funds up to 100% of approved capital costs; municipal program returns 40% of revenues to local cities
how_to_apply: Annual Call for Projects via the Safe, Clean Water Portal; technical and community scoring by Watershed Area Steering Committees
cycle_dates: Annual call opens spring; deadline July 31

verification.method: Public Works' 17 July 2018 Board letter (revised), which carries the proposed Chapter 16 ordinance and the program elements; safecleanwaterla.org still returns 403
verification.evidence: file.lacounty.gov/SDSInter/bos/supdocs/124293.pdf (fetched 2026-11-16): 'Forty percent (40%) shall be allocated to Municipalities within the District, in the same proportion as the amount of revenues collected within each Municipality'; 'Fifty percent (50%) shall be allocated to ... the Regional Program'; 'Ten percent (10%) shall be allocated to the District'; 'funding for Projects that provide a DAC Benefit is not less than one hundred ten percent (110%) of the ratio of the DAC population to the total population in each Watershed Area'; 'The initial Threshold Score is sixty (60) points'; scoring table 'Total Points All Sections 110'.
verification.notes: Round 3: safecleanwaterla.org 403; dpw.lacounty.gov alternate 403. Round 4 (2026-11-16): allocation, DAC and scoring terms confirmed from the 2018 Board letter; the record's 'up to 100% of capital costs' and the July 31 deadline are not in it.

40% municipal return.quote: Forty percent (40%) shall be allocated to Municipalities within the District, in the same proportion as the amount of revenues collected within each Municipality

statutory_citation.quote: This ordinance amends the Los Angeles County Flood Control District Code by adding Chapter 16 establishing the Los Angeles Region, Safe, Clean Water Program and imposing a special parcel tax within the Los Angeles County Flood Control District
statutory_citation.note: The letter is the proposal placed before the Board for the November 2018 ballot; the adopted text and later amendments were not fetched.

program_name: CAL FIRE Urban & Community Forestry Grants
administering_agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (CAL FIRE)
statutory_citation: Cal. Pub. Res. Code § 4799.06 et seq. (California Urban Forestry Act of 1978); grants under § 4799.12
eligible_improvements: Urban tree planting, care, and canopy maintenance in urban areas
Urban forest management plans and inventories
Green schoolyards and canopy shade over playgrounds
funding_share_description: Statute: grants of 25 to 90 percent of project costs; the director may waive cost sharing for projects in disadvantaged and low-income communities (PRC § 4799.12).

verification.method: California Legislative Counsel official bulk database (downloads.leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/pubinfo_2025.zip, LAW_SECTION_TBL, read via HTTP range requests; leginfo.legislature.ca.gov itself returns 403 from the audit container); PRC §§ 4799.06, 4799.12. fire.ca.gov returned 403
verification.evidence: § 4799.12: 'may make grants to provide assistance of 25 to 90 percent of costs ... may waive the cost sharing requirement for projects that are in disadvantaged and low-income communities'
verification.notes: Original '100% for DAC; up to 75% for non-DAC' contradicts the statute (25–90%, waivable).

program_name: Florida Live Local Act multifamily affordable-housing property tax exemption
administering_agency: Florida Department of Revenue and County Property Appraisers

verification.evidence: § 196.1978(3)(d)1.a: 'Seventy-five percent of the assessed value of the units ... greater than 80 percent but not more than 120 percent'; DOR: 'DR-504AFH ... Multifamily Project and Affordable Housing Property ... (section 196.1978, F.S.)'
unverified_fields: eligible_improvements wording (project-size and new-construction conditions not checked)

program_name: Colorado Urban Renewal Authority (URA) Tax Increment Financing
administering_agency: Local Colorado Urban Renewal Authorities and Municipalities
eligible_improvements: Transit-oriented community infrastructure, environmental remediation, and multi-modal transit hubs
Utility capacity upgrades to support 40+ units/acre density near passenger rail under HB 24-1313
Public plazas, street trees, and protected pedestrian paths
funding_share_description: An urban renewal plan may divide property taxes and/or municipal sales taxes in the area for a period not to exceed 25 years; the increment over the base goes to a special fund for the project.
how_to_apply: Urban renewal plan adoption by city council with statutory blight/condition study and taxing entity agreements

verification.evidence: "property taxes ... or that municipal sales taxes collected within said area, or both such taxes ... must be divided for a period not to exceed twenty-five years after the effective date of adoption of such a provision"
verification.notes: Mechanism and 25-year limit confirmed. The '100% of increment' share and the listed eligible projects (incl. the HB 24-1313 density link) are not in the statute; share depends on agreements with taxing bodies.
